review: rework. Brief: all 8 units present, acceptance met but restore robustness; out_of_scope untouched. Direction: core only, src/app unchanged. Abstraction: store owned by World, cap named, reads allocate nothing, nothing per update. Tests: CI green on 1896ab5 (last code commit; 5ae1d4d docs-only, docs green); suites items/save/revisit cover the brief. Report: perf before/after present. Findings: 1. src/core/src/world_save.cpp:301 read_items walks the container chain with index_of.find(...)->second before every container is known to exist: hammer(1) in jug(2) in cabinet(3), save, forge the jug's container to 77, restore -> ASan stack-buffer-overflow (UB), not Corrupt. Check every thing's container in a first pass and walk chains in a second (or test find != end), and add that case to the Corrupt test in tests/core/test_save.cpp. 2. read_items refuses a repeated location by scanning every earlier listing (O(listings^2)), and restore merges moved listings with find_if over settled; a generated 2048-square stage would make load quadratic. Require listings in the writer's fixed order (strictly increasing, refuse otherwise) or use a sorted key set, and merge moved listings through a map. 3. Manual 'walk to the next stage once and confirm no crash' was not done: run it in the dev build and report the result.

review amended: finding 3 withdrawn and the brief's manual step 'walk to the next stage' dropped. The map is one continuous world (Ryan, 2026-10-14; ADR-0007, D-041); today's stage exit is a test placeholder that PEO-118 removes, and the revisit case already covers load_stage emptying the store. Findings 1 and 2 stand.

rework: (1) 1990d30 read_items checks every thing's container exists in a first pass, then walks chains in a second; 352426d adds the reviewer's case to the Corrupt test (hammer 1 in jug 2 in cabinet 3, jug's container forged to 77): on the old code it gives ASan stack-buffer-overflow at world_save.cpp:301, now Corrupt naming ITEM with the save bytes unchanged. (2) listings must come strictly in the writer's order (location_before, now a shared free function in item_store.hpp used by locations() too): one comparison per listing, and a repeat is refused; moved listings merge through std::map<Location, ..., LocationBefore>, so load is n log n. tests: verify.py --frontend --full all stages passed; the new cases still sum 7.0-9.1 ms under ASan over 5 runs (median 7.7). Finding 3 withdrawn by the architect
